subject: biology
title: Eye defects and their correction
key_idea: In short-sightedness light focuses in front of the retina, and a concave lens corrects it. In long-sightedness light focuses behind the retina, and a convex lens corrects it. In a cataract the lens turns cloudy, and surgery replaces it. (Separate science)

blocks.text: (Separate science) A clear image forms only if light is focused on the retina. In these two defects it is not.

rows: Eyeball too long, cornea too curved, or lens too powerful (cannot be made thin enough). Light is refracted too much.
Eyeball too short, or lens cannot be thickened enough (weak ciliary muscles or an inelastic lens).
**Convex (converging)**: bends the light rays inwards more
Contact lenses, or laser treatment of the cornea

items: A corrective lens in glasses or a contact lens changes the direction of the light rays before they enter the eye.
After correction, the light rays meet (converge) on the retina and a clear image forms.
Laser treatment reshapes the cornea, so light is refracted less before it enters the eye.
Short-sighted: far objects blurred, light focuses in front of the retina, concave lens.
Long-sighted: near objects blurred, light focuses behind the retina, convex lens.
The correct lens makes light focus on the retina.

blocks.text: (Separate science) These two defects have different causes. One affects the lens and the other affects receptor cells.

items: In a cataract, the lens becomes **cloudy**.
Less light reaches the retina, so the image is blurred and less clear.
Surgery treats cataracts. The surgeon cuts into the eye (or uses a laser) and removes the old lens.
It is replaced with a new clear artificial lens, made of plastic.
Eye drops are being developed. They carry less risk of infection and permanent damage, and need no surgery.
Cone cells in the retina are responsible for colour vision.
In colour blindness, some cone cells are missing or do not work properly, so some colours cannot be told apart.
There is no cure. Tinted or coloured filter lenses can help some people tell certain colours apart.

diagram.alt: A predictor: pick an eye defect and see its cause, what the person cannot do and how it is corrected.

options.label: Short-sightedness
results: Eyeball too long, or lens too powerful
options.explanation: A concave lens spreads the rays out first, so they meet on the retina.

options.label: Long-sightedness
results: Eyeball too short, or lens cannot be thickened enough
options.explanation: A convex lens bends the rays inwards, so they meet on the retina.

options.label: Cataract
results: Surgery to replace the lens with a clear artificial lens
options.explanation: The lens is the part that has gone wrong, so it is replaced.

options.label: Colour blindness
results: Some colours cannot be told apart
No cure. Tinted filter lenses may help tell some colours apart. A focusing lens does not fix it.
options.explanation: The problem is in the receptor cells, not in how light is focused.

items: A cataract is a cloudy lens. The lens is replaced.
Colour blindness involves the cone cells.
Match each defect to its cause and its correction.

checks.q: A person cannot read road signs from a distance. Name the eye defect and the type of lens that corrects it.
Explain why a cataract makes vision blurred.
checks.a: The lens becomes cloudy, so less light reaches the retina.

checks.q: Describe how a convex lens helps a long-sighted person.
checks.a: The convex (converging) lens bends the light rays inwards more, so the rays are focused on the retina.

light rays bent / refracted (inwards) more
light rays focused on the retina
the eyeball is too short or the lens cannot be thickened enough
the ciliary muscles are too weak or the lens is not sufficiently elastic
light focuses behind the retina / the image forms behind the retina

mistakes.wrong: In long-sightedness, light is focused in front of the retina.
mistakes.right: In long-sightedness the light focuses behind the retina (the image forms behind the retina).

mistakes.wrong: A concave lens is used to correct long-sightedness.
mistakes.right: A convex (converging) lens is used. It bends the light rays inwards more so they focus on the retina.

worked_example.question:
Long-sightedness can be corrected by wearing spectacles.

Describe how spectacle lenses can correct long-sightedness.
answer_points: The lens is convex (converging), thicker in the middle.
Light rays are bent (refracted) inwards more.
Light rays are focused on the retina, so a clear image forms.
worked_example.tip: One mark for the type of lens, one for the refraction and one for focusing on the retina.

exam_phrases: the lens becomes cloudy
less light reaches the retina
replace the (old / opaque) lens with a new clear artificial lens
light is focused in front of the retina
the eyeball is too long / the lens cannot be made thin enough
a diverging lens bends / refracts light rays outwards
so the light rays meet / converge / focus on the retina
less risk of infection / permanent damage

mistakes.wrong: A diverging lens refracts the light rays less.
mistakes.right: Refract light rays less is ignored. Say that a diverging lens bends or refracts the light rays outwards, so they focus on the retina.

mistakes.wrong: The picture is less clear because light cannot get to the retina.
mistakes.right: Both points are needed. The lens becomes cloudy, so less light reaches the retina.

mistakes.wrong: Short-sightedness happens because the eyeball is too short.
mistakes.right: A short-sighted eyeball is too long (or the cornea is too curved), so light focuses in front of the retina.

worked_example.question:
A person cannot see distant objects clearly.

Explain why this person cannot see distant objects clearly and how the problem can be corrected.
answer_points: Light is not focused on the retina. It is focused in front of the retina.
The eyeball is too long, or the cornea is too curved, or the lens cannot be made thin enough, so the light is refracted too much.
It is corrected with glasses or contact lenses that are concave (diverging), or with laser treatment of the cornea.
The correction refracts the light less before it enters the eye.
So the light is focused on the retina.
worked_example.tip: This is marked in levels. Explain the cause first, then the correction, and finish by saying the light is focused on the retina.

exam_phrases: short sighted / has myopia
eyeball is too long / lens is too powerful
light / rays refract too much
light / rays focused in front of the retina
(glasses / contact lenses) with concave lenses
laser eye surgery

mistakes.wrong: A person who finds it difficult to read road signs at a distance is long-sighted.
mistakes.right: If the wrong defect is named, no marks are given. Difficulty with distance is short-sightedness (myopia).

mistakes.wrong: Short-sightedness is treated with convex lenses.
mistakes.right: Short-sightedness is treated with concave lenses in glasses or contact lenses, or with laser eye surgery.

worked_example.question:
A person is finding it difficult to read road signs at a distance whilst driving.

Describe the eye defect this person could have.
answer_points: Any one from: the eyeball is too long; the lens is too powerful; light refracts too much; light is focused in front of the retina (not at the retina).
worked_example.tip: Myopia is also allowed. If the defect named is wrong, no marks are awarded for the explanation.
